test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A tap fills a cistern in 18 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 24 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = 4 (fill) − 3 (empty) = 1 unit/hour.

Total Capacity (LCM of 18, 24) = 72 units.

One-fourth of the tank = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 units.

Time taken = 18 units ÷ 1 unit/hour = 18 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling Tap (A) time = 18 hours, Emptying Tap (B) time = 24 hours.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time; Required Time = Required Work ÷ Net Efficiency.

 **Tap**
 **Time (hours)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 Tap A (Fill)
 18
 72
 +4

 Tap B (Empty)
 24
 −3

⇒ Net efficiency when both open = 4 + (−3) = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Work to be done = 1/4 × Total Capacity = 1/4 × 72 = 18 units.

⇒ Time required = 18 ÷ 1 = 18 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Work Done

When one pipe fills and another empties, net work per hour = (1/x − 1/y), where x is filling time and y is emptying time.

LCM Method

Always assume total capacity as the LCM of individual times to avoid working with complex fractions.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (+), whereas outlet/leakage pipes have negative efficiency (−).</p
